hero.title: Reduce uncertainty before it becomes delivery risk.
hero.intro: SDK makes the problem, decisions, responsibilities and evidence visible throughout an engagement. The process adapts to the system, but the client always knows what is being decided and what comes next.

entryPaths.heading: The first step depends on what you already know.
entryPaths.intro: Starting implementation too early makes uncertainty expensive. Starting with another generic discovery exercise wastes time when the outcome is already clear.

items.title: The outcome is defined
items.copy: The system boundary, desired change and acceptance conditions are understood. We validate assumptions, compose the delivery team and plan the workstream.

items.title: The problem is visible, but the path is not
items.copy: The system is creating cost, risk or delay, but the cause or responsible response is unclear. We begin with a bounded technical assessment.

process.heading: Four stages, each ending in a decision.
process.intro: Progress is not measured by activity alone. Each stage produces evidence the client can review before more commitment is made.

items.title: Understand
items.purpose: Establish what the business needs, what the system does today and where uncertainty sits.
activities: Inspect the relevant system and operating context
Define success, access and known unknowns
items.output: A concise problem definition, current-state view and proposed scope.
items.decision: Is there enough evidence to design the response?

items.title: Design
items.purpose: Turn the problem into technical options, delivery boundaries and explicit trade-offs.
activities: Identify risks, dependencies and migration steps
items.output: A technical approach, decision record, milestones and acceptance criteria.
items.decision: Is this the right approach and commitment?

items.title: Build
items.purpose: Deliver the agreed change while keeping quality, risk and progress visible.
activities: Record decisions, evidence and unresolved risks
items.output: Working changes, review evidence and current operational documentation.
items.decision: Does the increment meet its acceptance conditions?

items.title: Handover
items.purpose: Place the system and the knowledge needed to operate it under client control.
activities: Transfer context to the people retaining ownership
items.output: Client-controlled code, infrastructure, documentation and agreed follow-up actions.
items.decision: Can the client operate and evolve the delivered scope?

responsibility.heading: The team can change with the work. Responsibility does not disappear between specialists.
responsibility.body: SDK selects independent specialists for the disciplines an engagement requires and coordinates them through one delivery framework. Decisions, access, documentation and work status are kept visible so knowledge does not remain with one individual.

items.title: SDK
items.copy: Defines the engagement framework, coordinates delivery and remains accountable for the quality controls agreed with the client.

items.title: Specialists
items.copy: Contribute the experience required by the system and work within shared decisions, review practices and acceptance criteria.

items.title: Client
items.copy: Provides business context, system access and timely decisions while retaining control of its repositories, infrastructure and information.

items.title: Shared record
items.copy: Keeps architecture decisions, risks, progress and operating knowledge accessible beyond any single contributor.

quality.heading: Confidence comes from mechanisms you can inspect.
quality.intro: We avoid unqualified promises such as secure, scalable or production-ready. The engagement defines how those qualities will be examined and evidenced for the system in question.

items.title: Written decisions
items.copy: Material architecture and scope choices record the context, trade-offs and consequences instead of disappearing into meetings.

items.title: Reviewable increments
items.copy: Work is divided into changes that can be inspected, tested and accepted before risk accumulates.

items.title: Appropriate verification
items.copy: Tests, security checks, performance evidence and deployment controls are selected according to the actual failure risk.

items.title: Operational ownership
items.copy: Documentation, access, recovery steps and unresolved risks are treated as delivery work, not optional material after launch.

scope.heading: Surface the change. Explain the consequence. Decide before proceeding.
scope.body: Existing systems reveal information as they are inspected and changed. When an assumption fails or a new dependency appears, SDK records the evidence, explains its effect on scope, risk and sequence, and asks for a decision. The change does not disappear into an invoice or a delayed handover.
steps: Explain the technical and commercial consequence

cta.title: Start with the uncertainty that is blocking the work.
cta.body: Tell us what is known, what is under pressure and what decision your organization needs to make next.
cta.label: Discuss the situation
